transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, basically what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I manage a sales team, and when I'm doing the sales reports, I'll do things like... well, I'll copy the wrong numbers right off the team dashboard. Or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. 

It's really frustrating because I'll think I went over everything perfectly fine, but then the mistakes are just sitting right there. It's starting to become a real problem.
Have you noticed that you're having trouble staying focused or are easily distracted, especially when you're working on tasks like these sales reports?

Yeah, definitely. Um, it happens a lot. When I'm trying to review the call notes or look over the numbers for those reports, it really doesn't take much to lose my focus. 

Like, if there's just one conversation going on across the room, or even if a random thought pops into my head about something I need to do at home... it just pulls me completely off track. And the frustrating part is I usually don't even notice I've stopped working until a few minutes have gone by.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily in situations outside of work, like when you're reading, driving, or having conversations?

Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed it being much of a problem outside of work, to be honest. 

Like, driving seems fine, and when I'm talking to my friends or my wife, I think I keep up okay. I don't read a whole lot anyway, so it's hard to say with that one. But yeah, mostly it's just the office stuff where I really notice it happening.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, especially in situations where you're supposed to stay seated, like during meetings or at your desk?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially in meetings. Sitting through a long meeting is... well, it feels like my body is just buzzing inside. 

I can't just sit there. I have to keep shifting around in my chair, or I'll be tapping my foot the whole time. Sometimes it gets so uncomfortable that I just have to make up an excuse to get up and walk out for a minute, just to move around. It's really hard to just stay put at my desk for too long, too.
Have you noticed these attention or restlessness issues in other settings, like at home or during social events, even if they're not as severe as at work?

Yeah, I guess it does show up at home, too, just maybe in a different way. Like, at work, it's really bad—it actually got to the point where my manager brought it up in my formal review, which wasn't great to hear. 

But at home... it's more about the follow-through. I'll say I'm going to do something, and then I just get sidetracked or forget, and it definitely causes some arguments. My wife and others, they just feel like they can't count on me to actually finish what I start. So, yeah, it definitely affects things outside the office, too.
When did you first start noticing these issues with attention and restlessness? Were they present in your childhood, or did they develop more recently?

I was definitely like this as a kid, too. Um, my mom actually still talks about it sometimes. She says she used to get notes from my teachers all the time back in elementary school. 

They were always saying how I rushed through my work, or that I lost my homework again. And they'd mention that I talked out of turn a lot, and that I just couldn't stay in my seat unless they kept reminding me to sit down. So, yeah, it's not really a new thing for me. I guess it's just always been there.
Do you feel that these issues with attention and restlessness have significantly affected your ability to function in multiple areas of your life, like work, relationships, or daily responsibilities?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, like I mentioned before, it's really causing problems across the board. At work, it's not just a minor annoyance—my manager actually put it in my formal performance review, which is pretty serious for me. And then at home... well, it just adds to the conflict. My wife and other people in my life, they just feel like they can't count on me to follow through on things. So, yeah, it's definitely affecting my ability to function in both places.
Can you give me a specific example of a time when your attention issues affected something you were doing at home or in a social setting?

Well, it's just regular life stuff, mostly. Like... I'll completely forget to return important calls. My attorney called a while back, and I just kept forgetting to call him back. Or bills—I'll forget to pay a bill until I get a late notice in the mail. And with my kids, I'll tell them I'm going to bring something home for them, and then I just show up empty-handed because it completely slipped my mind. It just happens all the time with things like that.
How long have you been experiencing these issues with attention and restlessness?

Well, like I said, it's always been there since I was a kid, but... as far as it being a major issue like this, it's really been a problem since I moved into my current supervisor role. That was about, I'd say, a year and two months ago. Before that, I could kind of manage it, but since taking on that position, it's just been a lot harder to keep up.
Have you ever noticed these issues affecting you in social situations, like when you're out with friends or at family gatherings?

I don't really know if it affects me socially, to be honest. I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed it being a big problem when I'm just hanging out with friends or at family things. The main issues are really just at work and with my wife and kids, like I was saying. Socially... it doesn't seem to get in the way as much.
Can you think of any situations outside of work and home, like at social events or in structured activities, where your attention or restlessness has caused a problem for you?

Well, if you mean structured things... yeah, I guess so. Even when I'm just trying to relax quietly, it's a struggle. Like, if I'm watching a movie with my kids or sitting through a service at church, I can't just sit there. I end up whispering comments to whoever is next to me, or I'm constantly checking my phone. Or I'll just get up and walk out for no real reason. I just have a really hard time staying put and being quiet in those kinds of situations.
Would you say that your difficulties are mainly with attention and focus, without significant problems related to being overly active or impulsive?

No, I wouldn't say that. I definitely have problems with being restless and impulsive, too. Like I was just saying about church or movies, I can't sit still, and I end up talking when I shouldn't or just getting up and walking away. So it's not just the focus part, it's the physical restlessness and, you know, doing things without thinking them through, too. Both sides of it are definitely a problem for me.
Have you ever had trouble with these issues in settings like school, public places, or during structured activities such as appointments or meetings with other groups?

I mean, I think I kind of just mentioned that with the church and movie examples. Those are the main public places or structured things where it really hits me. As for school, that was a long time ago, and honestly, I don't really remember it being a huge issue back then. Or at least, I don't remember it standing out. But yeah, like I said, it's mostly just sitting through things like church or a movie where I really struggle in public.
Have you noticed any problems with attention or restlessness in other public or structured settings, like during appointments, in meetings with groups, or at events like weddings or conferences?

Honestly, not really. I feel like I kind of just covered the main ones with the church and movie examples. I don't really go to conferences or big events like that anyway. And for regular appointments... they usually aren't long enough for me to get too antsy, I guess. So, no, nothing else really comes to mind for those kinds of places.
